source: Original items built on the four energies in Roger Hamilton's Wealth Dynamics: Dynamo (ideas and creating), Blaze (people and connection), Tempo (timing and the senses), Steel (detail and systems). Each answer adds to one energy; the two strongest set the profile. A free self-check, not the official Wealth Dynamics test.

items.say: When a new project starts, which part do you naturally grab?

options.text: Working out the plan, the numbers and the system
Getting the right people excited and on board
Coming up with the idea and the first version
Getting stuck in, sensing what's needed and starting the work

items.say: What do people most often thank you for?

options.text: Connecting them with someone, or lifting their spirits
Being steady and reliable when things got busy
Spotting the detail everyone else missed
A fresh idea that got them unstuck

items.say: Which kind of day leaves you feeling most alive?

options.text: A day full of conversations and people
Starting new things and seeing possibilities
Deep, quiet work on the details
Steady doing, with a good rhythm and things getting finished

items.say: When something goes wrong, what's your first move?

options.text: Find the facts and fix the process
Stay calm, read the situation, and wait for the right moment
Look for a whole new way to do it
Pick up the phone and talk it through

items.say: Where do you create your best value, or make your best money?

options.text: Being in the right place at the right time, and acting on it
Creating something new: a product, an idea, a piece of work
Through relationships, reputation and being out front
Owning and improving systems or assets over time

items.say: In a team, which role do you end up in?

options.text: The one who makes sure it actually gets done, on time
The one who builds the process so it runs without them
The one with the ideas and the vision
The one who keeps everyone connected and motivated

items.say: What gets in your way most often?

options.text: Getting pulled into too many conversations
Getting lost in the detail and missing the bigger picture
Waiting too long because the timing doesn't feel right
Starting more than I finish

items.say: How do you prefer to make a decision?

options.text: Look at the data
Gut feel for what's possible
Feel out the timing and the situation first
Talk it through with people I trust

items.say: What do you notice first when you walk into a room?

options.text: Who's there and how they're feeling
The mood and the pace of the room
What could be done differently here
What's out of place or not working

items.say: Which compliment lands best with you?

options.text: Everyone loves working with you
Your work is precise and thorough
You're the one I can always count on
That's brilliant, I'd never have thought of that

items.say: If you had a free month to build something, you'd most likely...

options.text: Set up a system or an investment that keeps paying off
Invent something that doesn't exist yet
Bring people together around a cause or an event
Help out somewhere hands-on and learn by doing
My numbers
My people
My senses and my timing
My imagination
